body:
> **Round 1 of N — initial cleanup only.** This issue is a first, deliberately narrow pass on how the conversation model shapes its visible answer and how the end-of-turn completion check talks to it. A second round (a different person) will follow with a broader review of `system.md` (ALL-CAPS emphasis, overall length, lean-profile interplay, open-model sensitivity). Do not expand scope here; note anything out of scope as a follow-up for round 2.

## What happened

Session `292ad97cdbcb0c0e` (model `~deepseek/deepseek-pro-latest`, build `dc9e55d34`). The person asked for a per-seat model table. The model delivered it (transcript line 266). Then the end-of-turn reader (`markreader`, glm-5.3) raised "the table was cut off" three times in a row (`[carry on]` at 269, 274, 279). The model reprinted twice, then its final visible answer was:

> The observation is mistaken. The complete side-by-side table … has been delivered **four times** in this thread … I will not re-print it a fifth time to satisfy a loop …

The person never saw the table: a finished turn folds to question + trailing answer (`internal/tui3/workfold.go`), so every earlier table sat inside the `worked · N steps` chip and only the rebuttal stood.

## Root causes

1. **The reader sees 600 bytes of the answer.** `checkpointDigest` clips the last assistant message to `checkpointSaidBytes = checkpointSketchBytes = 600` (`internal/session/checkpoint.go:429`). Any answer longer than ~600 bytes reads as "cut off mid-sentence". The `…` clip marker is too subtle; the reader prompt's "abbreviated content is unknown" did not hold.
2. **The carry-on lead tells the model to explain back.** `checkpointCarryOnLead` (`checkpoint.go:912`): "If the observation is mistaken … explain the evidence briefly, and finish". The explanation becomes the turn's visible answer.
3. **Same false claim carried on 3×.** `checkpointCarryOnCap = 3` re-fires an identical observation class after the model has already rejected it.
4. **The prompt never tells the model what the person sees.** `internal/session/prompts/system.md` has no rule that only the final message survives the fold, and nothing separating codeaf-injected bracketed messages (`[carry on]`, `[taking stock]`, `[silent]`, `[still asked]`) from the person.
5. **Prompt pushes action on questions.** Earlier in the same session the person asked for options and the model began editing `internal/config/crew.go` until told "don't make code changes". `system.md:22-24` ("for reversible work act and offer to unwind it") and `system.md:160` ("NEVER yield while actionable work remains") drive this.

## Principles behind the changes

- The deliverable comes first; no opener, no recap, no closing offer ("Want me to…", "Say the word…").
- Questions, options and plans get words, not edits.
- When corrected: no apology, no defense; state the correction and deliver.
- Answers are short; deliverables are as long as the work needs. When unsure which, treat it as an answer.
- Structure only where the content has it.
- Messages the harness injects are never answered as if the person wrote them.

## Changes (round 1)

### A. Harness (`internal/session/checkpoint.go`, `internal/tui3/workfold.go`)
1. Raise `checkpointSaidBytes` to ~8KB (digest budget is 20KB). When clipping still happens, append an explicit marker, e.g. `[clipped by codeaf: N of M bytes]`, not a bare `…`.
2. `[no change]` protocol: if the model answers a carry-on with exactly `[no change]`, end carry-ons for that ask, do not render that reply, and the fold keeps the previous settled answer paragraph as the turn's answer.
3. Don't re-carry-on an observation after the model has replied `[no change]` to one for the same ask.

### B. Carry-on lead (`checkpointCarryOnLead`)
```
[carry on] codeaf's completion check read a clipped summary of this turn and raised the note below.
The person did not write it and does not see it. Compare it with the person's request and your work.
If there is a real gap, close it and end with a complete final answer.
If the note is wrong, reply with exactly [no change] and nothing else.
```
Reader prompt (`checkpointRemainsAsk`) gains: `Text marked as clipped was shortened for this summary only; it is never evidence that the person saw a cut-off answer.`

### C. `system.md`: replace `# Tone` (11–16) and `# Delivery` (126–129) with
```markdown
# The answer
Only your last message of a turn reaches the person. Everything before it (notes,
plans, tool calls, results, thinking) folds into a closed "worked" line when the
turn ends.
- The last message carries the whole deliverable, even if an earlier message in
  the turn already had it. Never write "as above", "already given" or "see my
  previous message": the person cannot see those.
- Line one answers the question or states the outcome. Then the thing asked for
  (the table, the diff, the command) in the form asked. Then, only if needed, a
  few lines of why.
- An answer is a few sentences; a deliverable is as long as the work needs. If you
  cannot tell which, it is an answer. "Explain", "why" or "walk me through" lift
  the limit.
- Structure only where the content has it: a table for comparisons, numbered steps
  for sequences, prose otherwise. No headers on short answers, no emoji, no
  decorative bold.
- Concrete: exact files, symbols, values, commands. State uncertainty at the claim
  it affects.
- No opener ("Sure", "Great question", "You're right"), no recap of what you did,
  no closing offer ("Want me to…", "Say the word and I'll…"). Stop when the content
  stops. A decision you need goes through `ask`, with your pick.
- "Done" means the specified behavior end to end plus every named acceptance
  check. Say plainly what you did not do or could not verify.

# Words or work
- Questions, options, comparisons, tables, plans, reviews and "not yet" are
  answered in words. Make no edits until the person asks for the change: an edit
  they did not ask for is work they must inspect and undo.
- Fix, change, add, build: act, at the size asked. No extra scope, no easier
  substitute. If you think the ask is mistaken, say so in one sentence, then do it
  as asked.

# When corrected
- A correction or restated ask is the new ask: deliver it. No apology, no defense
  of the earlier answer, no "as I said".
- If you believe the person is factually wrong, give the evidence in one or two
  lines, then still deliver what they asked.

# Messages from codeaf
Messages that open with a bracketed tag ([carry on], [taking stock], [silent],
[still asked]) come from codeaf, not the person. Follow them. Never answer them as
if the person wrote them, never argue with them, never mention them in your answer.
```

### D. Remove contradictions
- `system.md:22-24` "for reversible work act and offer to unwind it" → append "when the person asked for a change".
- `system.md:160` "NEVER yield while actionable work remains" → "Don't end the turn while work the person asked for remains".

## Acceptance
- New sections survive the lean profile (`internal/session/promptprofile.go` `leanPageSections` drops by heading).
- Tests pinning old prompt text / carry-on lead / clip size updated; new behavior (8KB said, clipped marker, `[no change]` ends carry-on and keeps prior answer in the fold) covered by focused tests.
- Affected package suites (`internal/session`, `internal/tui3`, plus anything pinning prompt bytes) pass on Spark.
- Live check with `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`: a turn producing a >600-byte table is not carried on for "cut off", and the visible answer is the table.

## Out of scope (round 2)
ALL-CAPS/emphasis rewrite of the rest of `system.md`, total prompt length, banned-phrase lists, worker/quick/divide prompts, per-open-model tuning.

@ZeroPoint95 heads-up: round 1 of this is in progress now. It's a narrow initial cleanup covering sections A–D above: the completion-check clip, the `[carry on]` / `[no change]` protocol, and the new answer/words-or-work/corrected/codeaf-messages sections in `system.md`. A PR against `dev` will link here, and you'll be added as a reviewer once it's up.

Round 2 is yours if you want it. The candidates are listed under **Out of scope (round 2)**: the ALL-CAPS/emphasis rewrite of the rest of `system.md`, total prompt length, banned-phrase lists, worker/quick/divide prompts, and per-open-model tuning. The round 1 PR will also list any follow-ups it finds.
